Mosquito vectors transmit malaria, with infections linked to travel to Africa, Asia, India, and South America; imported cases occur among travelers returning home. Regional Rospotrebnadzor notes symptoms often do not appear immediately; incubation is typically 8–16 days but can extend up to three years. To reduce risk, travelers should start antimalarial chemoprophylaxis seven days before departure (prescribed by a doctor), continue during travel, and take medication for one month after returning. Preventive measures include mosquito nets, fumigants, bed canopies, long-sleeved clothing, and skin repellents. If fever rises long after travel, seek medical attention promptly and inform clinicians about trips to warm countries.

articleHeadline: Hepatitis A cases could rise in rainy season, virologist warns
articleSummary: Hepatitis A outbreaks could rise with the rainy season. Virologist Yong says this year's outbreak began in the hot season, signaling higher case numbers when rain arrives. The health ministry typically inspects affected areas and blames contaminated drinking water, but Yong notes inspections often occur later, after widespread transmission and high viral loads, making water tests more likely to detect the virus. He believes outbreaks often start with migrant workers introducing the virus into the country and then spreading in factories with many workers. He stresses hygiene in food-related factories and among restaurant staff, including strict handwashing after toilet use and vaccination for workers where possible. articleSummary: Ultrasound-assisted antiviral approach uses high-frequency sound waves (roughly 3-20 MHz) to induce resonance in viral particles, deforming or fragmenting the capsid and reducing infectivity. Advantages include non-invasive, localized treatment and reduced reliance on antivirals. Key challenges remain: many viruses replicate inside human cells where they are shielded; wave attenuation in tissue; precise calibration; and the lack of human clinical trials. The field sits within medical acoustics, with prior clinical uses like lithotripsy and high-intensity focused ultrasound.

articleHeadline: 함안군, 봄철 광견병 무료 예방접종···4월 29일
articleSummary: Rabies vaccination drive in Haman County, South Korea, on April 29, 2026, aims to prevent canine rabies. Free vaccination will be offered at each town office within the county, with morning sessions 10:00–11:00 for Daesan, Gunbuk, Beosu, Gaya, and Chilwon, and afternoon sessions 13:00–14:00 for Chilseo, Yeohang, Haman, Chilbuk, and Sanin. Dogs must be over 3 months old and have completed pet registration; unregistered dogs must register before vaccination. If attendance on April 29 is not possible, free vaccination is available through April 30 at local public-veterinary clinics. An Moon-jun, head of Haman County Agricultural Technology Center, emphasizes safety of pets and residents and invites broad participation since the service is free.
